Magical genes / 6 in this family

Colour modifiers

Genes with no shape of their own. Each reads what the horse already is and changes it - which is why they paint last, and why a plain horse shows some of them not at all.

An index. Each of these has its own page - that is where the inheritance table, the gene carrot and how you actually come by one live. The picture beside each name is that gene on a standard bay, baked through the real coat pipeline rather than drawn. A gene with no picture is one that changes no pixel of the coat - it does its work somewhere else.

Gamma

A chromatic modifier: diffuse fields of one saturated hue on the barrel and flank, each with a glow blooming past its edge - and nothing hard-edged anywhere on it.

Gam · n · full page

Invert

The last thing painted: the whole finished coat comes out as its own negative. White goes black, orange goes blue, and everything the horse was carrying goes with it.

Inv · n · full page

Nebula Light

Overlapping zones of magenta, violet, blue and teal across the back half of the horse, with a fine population of points through them and a few larger ones wearing halos.

Neb · n · full page

Opalized

The same substrate as Voided taken the other way - every white region comes out as iridescent cells of three to seven hues, pearlescent at the rim and strongest in the middle.

Opl · n · full page

Spectrum Light

One long field over the barrel and hip through which the hue rotates continuously in spectral order - red to violet, no bands, no repeats.

Spc · n · full page

Voided

Every white the horse would have had comes out black instead - the same markings, the same edges, the opposite pigment.

Vd · n · full page

The files

Each of these is a JSON file in common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/, listed in the index.json beside them and loaded by Genes' class initialiser. None is a Java class; see the gene file format for what the masks and ops mean.
